rationale: Quinbrook identifies PurposeEnergy as the manager-level portfolio company and Minster as one of its projects. Official local records identify PurposeEnergy - Minster LLC as the project/site entity; Danone is a commercial counterparty, and no distinct sponsor mandate, co-owner, later equity transfer or pending sale was found.
recommendedChanges: Merge/remove the standalone PurposeEnergy Minster PortCo record into PurposeEnergy.
Preserve PurposeEnergy - Minster LLC as the project/SPV identity and retain the Ohio site, Danone relationship, 250,000 GPD input and 50,000 MMBtu-per-year output facts.
Treat April 12, 2023 as the PurposeEnergy platform acquisition announcement, not as a separately proven legal closing date for Minster.
Record July 16, 2026 as first waste intake and ramp-up, not as confirmed full commercial operation.
Do not treat Danone, the Village of Minster, lenders or tax-credit counterparties as equity owners.
unresolvedQuestions: The immediate LLC member, exact stake, formation date and intermediate ownership chain are not publicly disclosed.
The PurposeEnergy legal closing date, seller cap table and exact Net Zero Power Fund sleeve are not publicly disclosed.
Full COD and Minster-specific financing parties are not publicly disclosed.
fieldCorrections: Do not present the platform acquisition announcement as a proven legal close.
Do not present first waste intake during ramp-up as confirmed full COD.
